terms.latin: nōn sōlum (nōn modo, nōn tantum) … sed (vērum) etiam
terms.grammar: adverbs and conjunctions; etiam may be left out or replaced by et
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.100: nōn sōlum in praesentiā, sed etiam posterō diē
Plin. NH 9.24: nōn hominī tantum amīcum animal, vērum et mūsicae artī
terms.comment: Where the first member is negative, “not only not … but even”: nōn modo … nōn …, vērum etiam; and “not only not … but not even”, nōn modo nōn … sed nē … quidem.

evidence: Liv. 26.50.13: vincentem omnia cum armīs, tum benignitāte ac beneficiīs

phrases.latin: vestrae quidem cēnae nōn sōlum in praesentiā, sed etiam posterō diē jūcundae sunt
phrases.english: your dinners are pleasant not only at the time but on the next day as well

phrases.latin: delphīnus nōn hominī tantum amīcum animal, vērum et mūsicae artī
phrases.english: the dolphin, an animal friendly not only to man but also to the art of music

phrases.latin: senectūs nōn modo languida atque iners nōn sit, vērum etiam sit operōsa et semper agēns aliquid et mōliēns
phrases.english: old age is not only not sluggish and idle, but is even busy, always doing and building something
